clue.text: 'The Samurai' cast is unprofessional

indicators.note: cast in the sense of thrown about or moulded anew, so the title's letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A film critic sneers that the Japanese epic The Samurai is a poorly made, unprofessional production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' reads as the film's actors, but it signals that THE SAMURAI is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: work that is unprofessional looks like that of a dabbler rather than an expert.

clue.text: Swords and shield motif?

definitions.meaning: swords and other weapons are collectively weaponry
the heraldic design borne on a shield, a coat of heraldry

explanation.surface: Swords and a shield design, the kit of a knight.
explanation.definitionFit: Weapons are arms, and a heraldic shield's design is a family's coat of arms.

clue.text: Turns up at Tottenham initially to head goals

indicators.note: to head means the preceding letters go in front of the next piece
initially picks the opening letter of the football club's name

parts.note: goals are aims or ends

explanation.surface: A footballer arrives at Tottenham's ground and starts heading in goals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to head' places the T from Tottenham in front of ENDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone who turns up at an event is present there, i.e. is there in person.

clue.text: Note very loud Scene VI set out to provide potency

parts.note: E is one of the musical notes
FF, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud

indicators.note: out as in disordered or put out of place, so the scene words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A stage direction: a loud note sounds as the sixth scene is set up, to give the play force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges SCENE VI SET into ECTIVENESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: potency is the power to produce an intended result, which is efficacy.

clue.text: Metres to helter-skelter? Extremely far

indicators.note: helter-skelter means in wild disorder, so the letters are thrown into confusion

explanation.surface: How many metres to the fairground helter-skelter slide? A very long way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'helter-skelter' looks like the fairground slide but is the anagram signal for METRES TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Superlative of remote: most distant, so extremely far away.

clue.text: American-backed and unstable Arab republic

indicators.note: backed read as moved backwards, so the two letters are turned round

parts.note: US is short for American, as in the United States

indicators.note: unstable means not settled, so the little word is jumbled

explanation.surface: A news report about an unstable Arab state propped up by Washington.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns US to SU; 'unstable' jumbles AND to DAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the country south of Egypt is a republic and a member of the Arab League.

clue.text: A religious sitcom returning as a police TV drama

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: Rev is a BBC sitcom about an inner-city vicar

explanation.surface: A TV schedule note: a vicar comedy comes back on air, billed as a detective series.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' reverses A REV. Rev was a BBC sitcom about a London vicar; the answer is an ITV detective series set in Northumberland.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a long-running ITV detective series named after its dogged Northumbrian inspector.

clue.text: Sleep it off is the message

indicators.note: off as in gone bad or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to someone who has overindulged: sleeping it off is the answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' looks part of the phrase 'sleep it off' but signals that SLEEP IT is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a formal letter, especially one of the New Testament letters, carries a message.

clue.text: Rub out a thin line scrawled around answer

indicators.note: around means the jumbled letters go round the next piece
scrawled means written messily, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Instructions to erase a faint line someone scribbled round an answer on a test paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrawled' jumbles A THIN LINE into ANNIHILTE, which goes 'around' A.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to rub someone out is slang for to kill, so to destroy utterly.

clue.text: Match award to be brought back? It's a theme you might hear more than once

definitions.text: a theme you might hear more than once

indicators.note: brought back means returned, so these letters are read in the reverse direction

parts.note: to match is to fit or suit
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: Is a man-of-the-match prize to be revived? A refrain heard again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be brought back' reverses FIT OM. The Order of Merit is an exclusive British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a recurring melodic figure or idea in music or literature, heard repeatedly.

clue.text: No time to study arbitration

indicators.note: No means without, so the next letter is dropped

parts.note: meditation is careful study or contemplation

explanation.surface: A busy negotiator laments having no time to study arbitration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No time' removes one T from MEDITATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: intervening to settle a dispute between parties, as arbitration does.

clue.text: Secretary's mounting support, helping to arrest one making embezzlement

indicators.note: mounting means climbing, so in a down answer the letters run upwards

parts.note: PA, personal assistant, is a secretary
a prop is a support

indicators.note: to arrest is to hold or capture, so the next piece is held inside

parts.note: a ration is a helping or portion
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A secretary's growing role, helping to arrest someone making off with funds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mounting' turns PA upwards to AP; RATION is made 'to arrest' I, giving RIATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: appropriation is taking money for one's own use, i.e. embezzlement.

clue.text: Nice point for a change in church — but means to quit?

indicators.note: for a change means altered, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: in and at both mean present somewhere, as in at home

explanation.surface: A debating point made in church, nicely, for a change, with a doubtful aside about giving up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for a change' rearranges NICE POINT into NICOTINEP.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a skin patch releasing the drug is one way a smoker gives up cigarettes.

clue.text: Bold, but not highly coloured?

definitions.meaning: read literally, not turning red in the face

explanation.surface: Is a bold person simply one whose cheeks never redden?
explanation.definitionFit: Literal and figurative: a shameless person shows no embarrassment, so their face never reddens.

clue.text: Article about Stones touring that is most unpleasant

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the article runs backwards

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the plural pieces go round the next

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the weight; two of them for the plural
IE, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece on the Rolling Stones' tour, that is, a nasty review.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns AN to NA; two STs (Stones) are 'touring' IE.
explanation.definitionFit: Superlative of nasty: nastiest is the most unpleasant of all.

clue.text: Peg gets left behind to prosper

indicators.note: behind means the next letter comes after the peg

parts.note: a dowel is a wooden peg

explanation.surface: A woodworking peg gets left behind on the bench.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to prosper is to thrive, succeed or flourish.

clue.text: Use garter to strangle

indicators.note: use means work or exploit, so the following letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A murderer's grim instruction to throttle a victim with a stocking band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Use' signals that GARTER TO is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to throttle with a cord or wire, an execution method.

clue.text: Bass apparently quiet

definitions.meaning: a bass part is pitched deep, so it is literally in a deep register
quiet in the sense of understated, restrained

explanation.surface: A bass singer seems subdued.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: something understated and restrained, rather than showy, is quiet.

clue.text: Stone Ron sculpted will make an impression

parts.note: Ron Wood is a guitarist in the Rolling Stones
sculpted means carved or cut

explanation.surface: A sculpture carved by the Rolling Stones guitarist is bound to impress.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'Stone' is a Rolling Stone, not a rock to carve.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a carved block of timber that is inked and pressed to print a picture.

clue.text: Where small kipper may be kept as bait to trap Young Conservative

definitions.text: Where small kipper may be kept

indicators.note: to trap means to hold, so the next letters sit inside

parts.note: a carrot is an inducement or bait
YC is short for Young Conservative, a UK party youth member

explanation.surface: A fishing image: smoked fish kept as bait to lure a young Tory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kipper' is a smoked herring on the surface but here is a sleeper, i.e. a baby.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a portable bed for a baby, a small sleeper.

clue.text: Take care pursuing prisoner with depression

indicators.note: pursuing means following, so this piece goes after

parts.note: a con is a convict
cave is Latin for beware, old school slang for take care

explanation.surface: A warning to watch out for a depressed escaped convict.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take care' is Latin 'beware', once a British schoolboy's lookout cry; 'pursuing' puts it second.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a concave surface curves inward, having a hollow or dip.

clue.text: Screen fitted to conceal washers

parts.note: washers are people washing; a screen in the bathroom hides them

explanation.surface: A fitted screen hiding the washing machines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'washers' suggests machines or plumbing rings, but means people bathing.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a waterproof drape hung around a bath or cubicle to give privacy.

clue.text: Ignore the odds to score first-class century for fun

indicators.note: ignore the odd-numbered letters, keeping only the even ones

parts.note: A1 means first-class, written AI
C is the abbreviation for century, a hundred

explanation.surface: A cricketer shrugs off the odds to hit a first-class hundred, just for fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ignore the odds' takes the second and fourth letters of 'score', CR. The answer is Irish for fun or good times.
explanation.definitionFit: Irish word: good company, lively talk and entertainment, i.e. fun.

clue.text: Criminal tendency

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: slang for crooked or corrupt, and a noun meaning an inclination or talent.

clue.text: Endless botched instances

indicators.note: botched means bungled, so the letters are messed up

explanation.surface: A complaint about one bungled case after another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'botched' rearranges INSTANCES.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: continuing without pause or interruption, never stopping.

clue.text: It's silly batting an eyelid to begin with

parts.note: a batter in cricket is in

indicators.note: to begin with picks the first letter of the eyelid word

explanation.surface: It's foolish to go out to bat without batting an eyelid.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the side batting is 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: silly, pointless, lacking sense.

clue.text: Cult follower in grand hot pants

parts.note: G is short for grand, a thousand pounds

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, signalling the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A cult devotee dressed in expensive, fashionable trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' (British slang for poor or rubbish) jumbles HOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a member of the dark-clad subculture, devoted to its music and style.

clue.text: Rocky sent secret audition

indicators.note: rocky means shaky, so the letters are shaken up

explanation.surface: Sylvester Stallone sent a secret tape to try out for the role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocky' looks like the film but means unsteady, rearranging SENT SECRET.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a filmed trial to see whether an actor suits a part.
